about: Source of truth for the physics scene templates. The backend reads it (validation, prompt, solver), the frontend reads it (drawing). A template is chosen by the model; its drawing and numbers are computed by code.

templates.title: Horizontal projection from a height (a ball thrown sideways off a tower or cliff)

elements.about: the ground line
the tower or cliff of the given height
the ball at the launch point
x horizontal, y vertical axes at the base of the tower
arrow for the horizontal launch speed
the parabolic trajectory
double arrow along the tower labelled h
double arrow along the ground labelled R
where the ball lands
arrow for the velocity at landing, with its components
the time of flight t shown beside the path

templates.title: Projectile launched at an angle (from the ground or from a height)

elements.about: the ground line
x horizontal, y vertical axes at the launch point
the ball at the launch point
arrow for the launch velocity u
arc and label for the launch angle
horizontal component u cos(theta)
vertical component u sin(theta)
the parabolic trajectory
the highest point
double arrow for the maximum height H
double arrow for the range R
where the ball lands

templates.title: Free-body diagram of one object with several forces

params.name: object
params.about: label of the object, e.g. block

params.name: forces
params.about: list of { label, magnitude (N), angle (deg, 0 = right, 90 = up) }

elements.about: the object drawn as a box or dot
arrow of the first force; force-2 to force-6 follow the order of the list
x and y axes through the object
the resultant force arrow

templates.title: Block on an inclined plane with weight, normal and friction

elements.about: the sloping surface and the ground
arc and label for the incline angle
the block resting on the slope
mg arrow pointing straight down
component of the weight along the slope
component of the weight into the slope
normal reaction arrow
friction arrow along the slope (only when mu is above 0)

templates.title: Velocity-time, position-time or acceleration-time graph built from straight segments

params.name: segments
params.about: list of { t0, t1, v0, v1 } in seconds and the graph's unit; segments follow each other

elements.about: labelled axes with ticks
the whole graph line
the first segment; segment-2 and so on follow the order of the list
shaded area under the graph (displacement for v_t)
a rise-over-run marker on the selected segment
